questions.question: Which Technology companies have shown the most consistent profitability improvement over the last 5 years (2019-2023)?
questions.business_context: Long-term profitability analysis for technology investment strategy and competitive positioning assessment

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Rank technology companies by 5-year profit margin improvement and monotonic consistency.
expected_answer.visualization: Line chart showing profit margin trends
expected_answer.business_insight: Semiconductor suppliers and recurring-revenue platforms are the only tech cohorts delivering four straight years of margin improvement; heavy transformation stories still show volatility but the slope is finally positive.
key_findings: ON Semiconductor expanded net profit margin from 3.84% in FY2019 to 26.46% in FY2023 (+22.62pp) thanks to silicon-carbide mix and disciplined capex, delivering 4/4 positive steps.
ADP inched margins from 16.17% to 18.94% with subscription automation and pricing lift—steady 0.5-0.7pp annual gains make it the benchmark compounder.
Uber swung from -60% to +5% margins as take rates and cost leverage improved post-pandemic; volatility remains but the profitability breakthrough is tangible.
Emerson’s FY2023 margin spike to 87.17% is tied to asset divestiture gains, highlighting the need to flag non-recurring uplift when ranking “improvements.”
investment_implications: Focus on firms showing structural, not just cyclical, margin expansion (ADP, ON Semi) for core holdings.
Turnaround names (Uber, First Solar) carry higher volatility but can rapidly add 25-65pp of margin once scale and mix inflect; size positions accordingly.
CFO teams should annotate one-time gains (e.g., Emerson disposals) before feeding automated storytellers, so downstream answers stay decision grade.
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH tech_companies AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cik, name
    FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/companies_with_sectors.parquet')
    WHERE gics_sector = 'Information Technology'
),
base_filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh, s.cik, CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year, s.period, s.filed,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/sub.parquet') s
    JOIN tech_companies t USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
),
filings AS (
    SELECT adsh, cik, fiscal_year, period
    FROM base_filings
    WHERE rn = 1
),
values AS (
    SELECT f.cik, f.fiscal_year,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'NetIncomeLoss' THEN n.value END) AS net_income,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') THEN n.value END) AS revenue
    FROM filings f
    JOIN read_parquet('data/parquet/num.parquet') n
      ON f.adsh = n.adsh AND n.ddate = f.period
    WHERE n.tag IN ('NetIncomeLoss','Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet')
    GROUP BY f.cik, f.fiscal_year
),
margins AS (
    SELECT t.name, v.cik, v.fiscal_year, v.net_income, v.revenue,
           v.net_income / NULLIF(v.revenue, 0) AS profit_margin
    FROM values v
    JOIN tech_companies t ON v.cik = t.cik
    WHERE v.net_income IS NOT NULL
      AND v.revenue IS NOT NULL
),
ordered AS (
    SELECT m.*,
           LEAD(m.profit_margin) OVER (PARTITION BY m.cik ORDER BY m.fiscal_year) AS next_margin,
           LEAD(m.fiscal_year) OVER (PARTITION BY m.cik ORDER BY m.fiscal_year) AS next_year
    FROM margins m
)
SELECT name,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 THEN profit_margin END)*100, 2) AS margin_2019_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN profit_margin END)*100, 2) AS margin_2020_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN profit_margin END)*100, 2) AS margin_2021_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2022 THEN profit_margin END)*100, 2) AS margin_2022_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN profit_margin END)*100, 2) AS margin_2023_pct,
       ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN profit_margin END) - MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 THEN profit_margin END))*100, 2) AS improvement_pct,
       SUM(CASE WHEN next_year = fiscal_year + 1 AND next_margin IS NOT NULL AND next_margin >= profit_margin THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS consistency_steps
FROM ordered
GROUP BY name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 5
ORDER BY consistency_steps DESC, improvement_pct DESC, name
LIMIT 5;

questions.question: Which companies across all sectors trimmed total debt the most between FY2021 and FY2023, and how does their year-by-year trajectory look?

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Rank companies by FY2021-FY2023 total debt reduction with year-by-year detail.
expected_answer.visualization: Waterfall chart showing debt reduction progression
expected_answer.business_insight: Corporate deleveraging since FY2021 has been led by balance-sheet intensive firms—AT&T, AIG, US Bancorp, Deere, and Apple collectively took $140B+ of debt off the books, freeing cash for dividends, buybacks, and reinvestment while reducing rate sensitivity.
key_findings: AT&T retired roughly $40B of debt post-WarnerMedia spin and fiber cash-flow ramp, keeping leverage within its 2.5x target range despite elevated capex.
AIG’s life-and-retirement divestitures converted into direct balance-sheet paydown, driving a 99% drop in reported debt and materially lowering interest expense.
US Bancorp and Deere each eliminated $27B-$29B of borrowings as funding costs rose, preserving flexibility for credit-cycle volatility.
Apple continued shrinking term debt (down $13.8B) even while returning cash to shareholders, using overseas cash repatriation and bond maturities.
Energy names like Occidental show sizable reductions as commodity cash flows were redirected from drilling toward balance-sheet repair.
investment_implications: Large-cap deleveraging is clustering in rate-sensitive sectors; investors can track debt reduction as a signal for future buyback capacity and dividend headroom.
Balance sheets that were right-sized early (AT&T, AIG) now have dry powder for M&A or accelerated network/technology spend without re-levering.
Banks that pre-funded growth (US Bancorp) mitigated regulatory capital pressure by shrinking wholesale debt, improving resilience ahead of tighter credit cycles.
Industrial names such as Deere that delevered while margins stayed high highlight disciplined capital allocation—an important screening factor for CFO offices.
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH company_dim AS (
    SELECT cik, name, gics_sector
    FROM (
        SELECT cik, name, gics_sector,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cik ORDER BY name) AS rn
        FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/companies_with_sectors.parquet')
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh, s.cik, CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year, s.period
    FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/sub.parquet') s
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2021 AND 2023
),
debt_inputs AS (
    SELECT f.cik,
           f.fiscal_year,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations','Totaldebtrecordeduponconsolidation') THEN n.value END) AS total_debt_tag,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('LongTermDebt','LongTermDebtNoncurrent','LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations','LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsNoncurrent','UnsecuredLongTermDebt','LongTermDebtOfConsolidatedInvestmentProducts') THEN n.value END) AS long_term_debt,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('DebtCurrent','ShortTermBorrowings','ShortTermBorrowingsIncludingLongTermDebtCurrent','ShortTermDebtAndCurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt','DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsCurrent') THEN n.value END) AS short_term_debt
    FROM annual_filings f
    JOIN read_parquet('data/parquet/num.parquet') n ON f.adsh = n.adsh AND n.ddate = f.period
    WHERE n.tag IN ('DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations','Totaldebtrecordeduponconsolidation','LongTermDebt','LongTermDebtNoncurrent','LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations','LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsNoncurrent','UnsecuredLongTermDebt','LongTermDebtOfConsolidatedInvestmentProducts','DebtCurrent','ShortTermBorrowings','ShortTermBorrowingsIncludingLongTermDebtCurrent','ShortTermDebtAndCurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt','DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsCurrent')
    GROUP BY f.cik, f.fiscal_year
),
total_debt AS (
    SELECT cik,
           fiscal_year,
            COALESCE(total_debt_tag, long_term_debt + COALESCE(short_term_debt, 0), long_term_debt, short_term_debt) AS total_debt
    FROM debt_inputs
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT td.cik,
           MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN total_debt END) AS debt_2021,
           MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2022 THEN total_debt END) AS debt_2022,
           MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN total_debt END) AS debt_2023
    FROM total_debt td
    GROUP BY td.cik
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 3
),
joined AS (
    SELECT cd.name,
           cd.gics_sector,
           debt_2021,
           debt_2022,
           debt_2023,
           (debt_2021 - debt_2023) AS debt_reduction
    FROM ranked r
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
)
SELECT name, gics_sector,
       ROUND(debt_2021/1000000, 2) AS debt_2021_m,
       ROUND(debt_2022/1000000, 2) AS debt_2022_m,
       ROUND(debt_2023/1000000, 2) AS debt_2023_m,
       ROUND((debt_2021 - debt_2023)/1000000, 2) AS reduction_m,
       ROUND(((debt_2021 - debt_2023) / NULLIF(debt_2021, 0)) * 100, 2) AS reduction_pct
FROM joined
WHERE debt_2021 IS NOT NULL AND debt_2023 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY reduction_m DESC
LIMIT 5;

questions.question: Which Healthcare companies improved their current ratios the most between FY2019 and FY2023?

expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH healthcare AS (
    SELECT cik,
           name,
           REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name
    FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/companies_with_sectors.parquet')
    WHERE gics_sector = 'Health Care'
),
filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh,
           s.cik,
           CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
           s.period,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/sub.parquet') s
    JOIN healthcare h USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
),
latest AS (
    SELECT adsh, cik, fiscal_year, period
    FROM filings WHERE rn = 1
),
ratios AS (
    SELECT h.canonical_name,
           h.name,
           lf.fiscal_year,
           (MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'AssetsCurrent' THEN n.value END) /
            NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'LiabilitiesCurrent' THEN n.value END), 0)) AS current_ratio
    FROM latest lf
    JOIN read_parquet('data/parquet/num.parquet') n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    JOIN healthcare h USING (cik)
    WHERE n.tag IN ('AssetsCurrent','LiabilitiesCurrent')
    GROUP BY h.canonical_name, h.name, lf.fiscal_year
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT canonical_name,
           ANY_VALUE(name) AS display_name,
           ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 THEN current_ratio END), 2) AS ratio_2019,
           ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN current_ratio END), 2) AS ratio_2020,
           ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN current_ratio END), 2) AS ratio_2021,
           ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2022 THEN current_ratio END), 2) AS ratio_2022,
           ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN current_ratio END), 2) AS ratio_2023,
           COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) AS year_count
    FROM ratios
    GROUP BY canonical_name
    HAVING year_count = 5
)
SELECT display_name AS name,
       ratio_2019,
       ratio_2020,
       ratio_2021,
       ratio_2022,
       ratio_2023,
       ROUND(ratio_2023 - ratio_2019, 2) AS improvement
FROM pivoted
WHERE ratio_2019 IS NOT NULL AND ratio_2023 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY improvement DESC
LIMIT 10;
expected_answer.business_insight: Medical device and animal health specialists posted the sharpest liquidity gains between FY2019 and FY2023 as pandemic demand, premium pricing, and disciplined inventory management expanded current ratios by 60–180 bps. Leaders such as Hologic and ResMed now operate with more than 3x coverage of short-term liabilities, giving CFO teams ample headroom for M&A and R&D without relying on external credit.
key_findings: Hologic’s current ratio nearly doubled (1.68→3.47) thanks to diagnostic cash inflows and leaner receivables.
ResMed maintained >3x liquidity while scaling ventilation capacity, showing sustained working-capital agility.
Zoetis and IDEXX grew ratios by 60–75 bps as pet-health demand accelerated and inventory turns improved.
Cooper Companies and STERIS moved from near-1.0x to well above 1.5x, removing prior liquidity constraints.
investment_implications: Device makers with >3x current ratios can self-fund tuck-in deals and platform upgrades even if rates stay elevated.
Improved working-capital cushions lower refinancing risk and provide shock absorbers for supply-chain disruptions.
Liquidity expansion highlights the health of recurring-revenue models in diagnostics, animal health, and vision care.

questions.question: Which Technology companies expanded operating margins the most between FY2022 and FY2023?

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Rank Technology companies by FY2022 vs FY2023 operating margin improvement (OperatingIncomeLoss / Revenue).
expected_answer.format: Table with FY2022 margin, FY2023 margin, and percentage point delta
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_companies AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cik, name
    FROM companies
    WHERE gics_sector = 'Information Technology'
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh, s.cik, CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year, s.period,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy IN (2022, 2023)
),
latest AS (
    SELECT adsh, cik, fiscal_year, period
    FROM annual_filings
    WHERE rn = 1
),
values AS (
    SELECT lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'OperatingIncomeLoss' THEN n.value END) AS operating_income,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') THEN n.value END) AS revenue
    FROM latest lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    WHERE n.tag IN ('OperatingIncomeLoss','Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet')
    GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
agg AS (
    SELECT sc.cik, ANY_VALUE(sc.name) AS display_name,
           MAX(CASE WHEN v.fiscal_year = 2022 THEN v.operating_income / NULLIF(v.revenue, 0) END) AS margin_2022,
           MAX(CASE WHEN v.fiscal_year = 2023 THEN v.operating_income / NULLIF(v.revenue, 0) END) AS margin_2023,
           MAX(CASE WHEN v.fiscal_year = 2023 THEN v.revenue END) AS revenue_2023
    FROM values v
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    GROUP BY sc.cik
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT v.fiscal_year) = 2
)
SELECT display_name AS name,
       ROUND(margin_2022 * 100, 2) AS margin_2022_pct,
       ROUND(margin_2023 * 100, 2) AS margin_2023_pct,
       ROUND((margin_2023 - margin_2022) * 100, 2) AS improvement_pp,
       ROUND(revenue_2023 / 1000000000, 2) AS revenue_2023_b
FROM agg
WHERE revenue_2023 >= 5000000000
  AND margin_2023 IS NOT NULL AND margin_2022 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY improvement_pp DESC
LIMIT 10;
expected_answer.business_insight: Operating leverage gains clustered in large-cap technology platforms that either exited restructuring cycles (FIS, DoorDash) or monetized AI demand (NVIDIA, Palo Alto Networks). Salesforce and Meta achieved double-digit improvements after multi-quarter efficiency programs, proving that disciplined opex cuts now flow directly into operating income.
key_findings: FIS swung +126 percentage points as goodwill impairments rolled off and processing margins normalized after the fintech write-down.
NVIDIA converted datacenter-led revenue growth into a 35pp margin gain while holding operating expenses nearly flat.
Salesforce re-established mid-teens operating margins thanks to its FY2023 restructuring and mix shift toward high-margin subscription revenue.
Meta and DoorDash each improved by ~10pp despite very different models, showing that both AI-driven ad recovery and logistics scale can drive leverage.
Cybersecurity leader Palo Alto Networks crossed into positive operating margins as recurring platform revenue outpaced go-to-market spending.
investment_implications: Platforms that pair AI demand with cost discipline (NVIDIA, Palo Alto) demonstrate repeatable operating leverage and deserve premium multiples.
Turnaround names (FIS, DoorDash) proved that restructuring actions translated into tangible margin repair, de-risking 2024 guidance.
Double-digit improvements on $5B+ revenue bases highlight CFO playbooks that can be redeployed across adjacent sectors (software, payments, cybersecurity).

questions.question: Which Technology companies have shown declining ROE over the past 3 years even as revenue kept growing, and how large is the divergence between the two trends?

expected_answer.visualization: Side-by-side bars (ROE change vs revenue growth)
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_companies AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cik, name
    FROM companies
    WHERE gics_sector = 'Information Technology'
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh, s.cik, CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year, s.period,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2021 AND 2023
),
latest AS (
    SELECT * FROM annual_filings WHERE rn = 1
),
values AS (
    SELECT lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'NetIncomeLoss' THEN n.value END) AS net_income,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('StockholdersEquity', 'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest') THEN n.value END) AS equity,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') THEN n.value END) AS revenue
    FROM latest lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'NetIncomeLoss',
        'StockholdersEquity',
        'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest',
        'Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet'
    )
    GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
agg AS (
    SELECT sc.cik,
           ANY_VALUE(sc.name) AS name,
           MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN net_income / NULLIF(equity, 0) END) AS roe_2021,
           MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN net_income / NULLIF(equity, 0) END) AS roe_2023,
           MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN revenue END) AS revenue_2021,
           MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN revenue END) AS revenue_2023
    FROM values
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    GROUP BY sc.cik
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN fiscal_year IN (2021, 2023) THEN fiscal_year END) = 2
)
SELECT name,
       ROUND(roe_2021 * 100, 2) AS roe_2021_pct,
       ROUND(roe_2023 * 100, 2) AS roe_2023_pct,
       ROUND((roe_2023 - roe_2021) * 100, 2) AS roe_change_pp,
       ROUND(((revenue_2023 - revenue_2021) / NULLIF(revenue_2021, 0)) * 100, 2) AS revenue_growth_pct
FROM agg
WHERE revenue_2023 > revenue_2021
  AND roe_2023 < roe_2021
ORDER BY roe_change_pp ASC
LIMIT 10;

sample_data.primary_cause: Handset weakness plus elevated R&D cut asset efficiency faster than top-line grew.
Xilinx integration and datacenter capex drove equity base higher than earnings.
Cloud infrastructure build-out suppressed ROE despite accelerating subscription revenue.
Record buybacks moderated but supply chain investments lifted equity faster than profits.
Consumer cyber acquisitions expanded revenue yet goodwill/intangibles depressed ROE.

expected_answer.business_insight: Multiple large-cap Technology names grew revenue between FY2021 and FY2023 yet saw ROE compress sharply because reinvestment (M&A, cloud capex, R&D) expanded the equity base faster than earnings. Qualcomm and AMD exemplify how margin pressure plus higher working capital can erase ROE even when top-line momentum remains positive.
key_findings: Qualcomm’s ROE fell 57pp as Android demand weakened and modem R&D spend outpaced modest revenue growth.
AMD’s ROE nearly evaporated (28.6% → 1.4%) despite 38% sales growth because Xilinx dilution and datacenter buildouts lifted equity.
Oracle’s ROE dropped 24pp while revenue grew 23%—cloud infrastructure capex remains a drag until utilization scales.
Apple’s ROE remains triple digits but compressed ~19pp due to higher inventory buffers and continued silicon investment.
Gen Digital’s roll-up strategy grew revenue 36% but goodwill-heavy equity eroded ROE by 17.5pp.
investment_implications: Watch for firms where ROE erosion signals capital efficiency risk even when sales trends look healthy.
Cloud and AI buildouts can depress ROE for several years; investors should model a delayed return on incremental equity.
Software consolidators with goodwill-heavy balance sheets (e.g., Gen Digital) need disciplined integration to restore ROE.
Screening for “revenue up / ROE down” scenarios highlights where activist pressure or capital allocation pivots may emerge.

questions.question: Which Industrials compressed working capital days the most between FY2020 and FY2023, and what does that imply for their cash conversion cycles?

expected_answer.format: Working capital days table with optional CCC metrics
expected_answer.visualization: Slope chart showing working capital day reductions
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_companies AS (
    SELECT cik, name,
           REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name
    FROM companies
    WHERE gics_sector = 'Industrials'
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT s.adsh, s.cik, CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year, s.period,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2020 AND 2023
),
latest AS (
    SELECT * FROM annual_filings WHERE rn = 1
),
vals AS (
    SELECT lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'AssetsCurrent' THEN n.value END) AS assets_current,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'LiabilitiesCurrent' THEN n.value END) AS liabilities_current,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') THEN n.value END) AS revenue,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('InventoryNet','Inventory') THEN n.value END) AS inventory,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('AccountsReceivableNetCurrent','AccountsReceivableTradeCurrent') THEN n.value END) AS ar,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold','CostOfRevenue') THEN n.value END) AS cost_of_revenue,
           MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('AccountsPayableCurrent','AccountsPayableTradeCurrent') THEN n.value END) AS ap
    FROM latest lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'AssetsCurrent','LiabilitiesCurrent','Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet',
        'InventoryNet','Inventory','AccountsReceivableNetCurrent','AccountsReceivableTradeCurrent',
        'CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold','CostOfRevenue','AccountsPayableCurrent','AccountsPayableTradeCurrent'
    )
    GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
computed AS (
    SELECT
        v.cik,
        v.fiscal_year,
        (assets_current - liabilities_current) / NULLIF(revenue, 0) * 365 AS wc_days,
        inventory / NULLIF(cost_of_revenue, 0) * 365 AS dio,
        ar / NULLIF(revenue, 0) * 365 AS dso,
        ap / NULLIF(cost_of_revenue, 0) * 365 AS dpo
    FROM vals v
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        sc.canonical_name,
        ANY_VALUE(sc.name) AS name,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN wc_days END) AS wc_2020,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN wc_days END) AS wc_2023,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN (dio + dso - dpo) END) AS ccc_2020,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN (dio + dso - dpo) END) AS ccc_2023
    FROM computed c
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    GROUP BY sc.canonical_name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN fiscal_year IN (2020,2023) THEN fiscal_year END) = 2
)
SELECT name,
       ROUND(wc_2020,2) AS wc_2020_days,
       ROUND(wc_2023,2) AS wc_2023_days,
       ROUND(wc_2023 - wc_2020,2) AS wc_change_days,
       ROUND(ccc_2020,2) AS ccc_2020_days,
       ROUND(ccc_2023,2) AS ccc_2023_days,
       ROUND(ccc_2023 - ccc_2020,2) AS ccc_change_days
FROM agg
WHERE wc_2020 IS NOT NULL AND wc_2023 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY wc_change_days;
expected_answer.business_insight: Industrial working-capital discipline snapped back after the pandemic. Airlines and aerospace OEMs released more than 150 days of tied-up cash as travel demand normalized, while asset-light logistics and machinery names pared inventories and receivables. The mix shows that even companies with structurally negative short-term working capital (e.g., Delta posting negative days) rely on advance ticket sales to fund operations, whereas semiconductor equipment makers still carry high work-in-progress levels despite progress.
key_findings: Southwest and Boeing delivered the steepest working capital day reductions (285 and 153 days) as deferred revenue returned to balance sheets and supply chains stabilized.

annual_values AS (

         MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('DebtCurrent','ShortTermBorrowings','ShortTermDebtAndCurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt','CurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt') THEN n.value END) AS short_term_debt,
         MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue','CashCashEquivalentsAndShortTermInvestments') THEN n.value END) AS cash,
         MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('OperatingIncomeLoss','IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest') THEN n.value END) AS operating_income,
         MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN ('DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization','DepreciationAndAmortization','DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet') THEN n.value END) AS depreciation
  FROM latest lf
  JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
  WHERE n.tag IN (
    'LongTermDebt','LongTermDebtNoncurrent','LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations',
    'DebtCurrent','ShortTermBorrowings','ShortTermDebtAndCurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt','CurrentPortionOfLongTermDebt',
    'CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue','CashCashEquivalentsAndShortTermInvestments',
    'OperatingIncomeLoss','IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest',
    'DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization','DepreciationAndAmortization','DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet'
  )
    AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments),'') = ''
    AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg),'') = ''
  GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
metrics AS (
  SELECT cd.display_name AS company,
         fiscal_year,
         (COALESCE(long_term_debt,0) + COALESCE(short_term_debt,0)) AS gross_debt,
         COALESCE(cash,0) AS cash,
         (COALESCE(long_term_debt,0) + COALESCE(short_term_debt,0) - COALESCE(cash,0)) AS net_debt,
         operating_income + COALESCE(depreciation,0) AS ebitda,

           WHEN ABS(operating_income + COALESCE(depreciation,0)) < 100000000 THEN NULL

  FROM annual_values av

       ROUND(ebitda / 1e9, 2) AS ebitda_billions,
       ROUND(net_debt_to_ebitda, 2) AS net_debt_to_ebitda
FROM metrics
ORDER BY company, fiscal_year;

    SELECT adsh, cik, fiscal_year, period
    FROM annual_filings
    WHERE rn = 1
),
annual_values AS (
    SELECT
        sc.display_name AS company,
        sc.canonical_name,
        lf.cik,
        lf.fiscal_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'NetIncomeLoss',
            'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic',
            'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersDiluted'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS net_income,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'StockholdersEquity',
            'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS equity
    FROM latest_filings lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    JOIN company_seed sc USING (cik)
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'NetIncomeLoss',
        'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic',
        'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersDiluted',
        'StockholdersEquity',
        'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY sc.display_name, sc.canonical_name, lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
roe_values AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        fiscal_year,
        CASE
            WHEN net_income IS NULL OR equity IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN ABS(equity) < 100000000 OR equity <= 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE LEAST(
                150,
                GREATEST(
                    -150,
                    (net_income / NULLIF(equity, 0)) * 100
                )
            )
        END AS roe_pct
    FROM annual_values
),
filtered_years AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM roe_values
    WHERE fiscal_year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2024
      AND roe_pct IS NOT NULL
),
streak_index AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE WHEN roe_pct >= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS above_threshold,
        CASE
            WHEN roe_pct >= 15 THEN fiscal_year - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY canonical_name, CASE WHEN roe_pct >= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
                ORDER BY fiscal_year
            )
            ELSE NULL
        END AS streak_group
    FROM filtered_years
),
consecutive_runs AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length,
        MIN(fiscal_year) AS streak_start_year,
        MAX(fiscal_year) AS streak_end_year
    FROM streak_index
    WHERE above_threshold = 1
    GROUP BY canonical_name, streak_group
),
longest_streak AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        streak_length,
        streak_start_year,
        streak_end_year,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY canonical_name
            ORDER BY streak_length DESC, streak_end_year DESC
        ) AS streak_rank
    FROM consecutive_runs
),
company_longest AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        streak_length AS max_consecutive_years,
        streak_start_year,
        streak_end_year
    FROM longest_streak
    WHERE streak_rank = 1
),
roe_summary AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        ANY_VALUE(company) AS company,
        COUNT(*) AS years_reported,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE above_threshold = 1) AS years_above_threshold,
        ROUND(AVG(roe_pct) FILTER (WHERE above_threshold = 1), 2) AS avg_roe_pct,
        ROUND(
            COALESCE(
                STDDEV_SAMP(roe_pct) FILTER (WHERE above_threshold = 1),
                0
            ),
            2
        ) AS roe_volatility_pct,
        ROUND(MIN(roe_pct) FILTER (WHERE above_threshold = 1), 2) AS min_streak_roe_pct,
        ROUND(MAX(roe_pct) FILTER (WHERE above_threshold = 1), 2) AS max_streak_roe_pct,
        MIN(fiscal_year) AS first_year,
        MAX(fiscal_year) AS last_year
    FROM streak_index
    GROUP BY canonical_name
),
latest_values AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        CAST(fiscal_year AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        roe_pct,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY canonical_name
            ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM filtered_years
),
latest_per_company AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        fiscal_year AS latest_year_reported,
        ROUND(roe_pct, 2) AS latest_year_roe_pct
    FROM latest_values
    WHERE rn = 1
),
finalized AS (
    SELECT
        rs.company AS name,
        rs.canonical_name,
        rs.years_reported,
        rs.years_above_threshold,
        COALESCE(cl.max_consecutive_years, 0) AS max_consecutive_years,
        cl.streak_start_year,
        cl.streak_end_year,
        rs.avg_roe_pct,
        rs.roe_volatility_pct,
        rs.min_streak_roe_pct,
        rs.max_streak_roe_pct,
        rs.first_year,
        rs.last_year,
        lp.latest_year_reported,
        lp.latest_year_roe_pct
    FROM roe_summary rs
    LEFT JOIN company_longest cl USING (canonical_name)
    LEFT JOIN latest_per_company lp USING (canonical_name)
)
SELECT
    name,
    max_consecutive_years AS consecutive_years,
    years_above_threshold,
    years_reported,
    streak_start_year,
    streak_end_year,
    first_year,
    last_year,
    avg_roe_pct,
    roe_volatility_pct,
    min_streak_roe_pct,
    max_streak_roe_pct,
    latest_year_reported,
    latest_year_roe_pct
FROM (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY canonical_name
            ORDER BY
                max_consecutive_years DESC,
                avg_roe_pct DESC,
                roe_volatility_pct ASC,
                name
        ) AS name_rank
    FROM finalized
    WHERE max_consecutive_years >= 3
      AND years_above_threshold >= 3
      AND years_reported >= 3
      AND avg_roe_pct IS NOT NULL
)
WHERE name_rank = 1
ORDER BY
    consecutive_years DESC,
    avg_roe_pct DESC,
    roe_volatility_pct ASC,
    name
LIMIT 10;

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Ranked table of free cash flow retention versus capital expenditure intensity
expected_answer.visualization: Dual metric heatmap (FCF retention vs capex intensity)
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cik,
        name AS display_name,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cik ORDER BY name) AS rn
    FROM companies
    WHERE ('Health Care' = 'ALL' OR UPPER(gics_sector) = UPPER('Health Care'))
),
company_seed AS (
    SELECT cik, display_name, canonical_name
    FROM sector_companies
    WHERE rn = 1
),
ranked_filings AS (
    SELECT
        s.adsh,
        s.cik,
        CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        s.period,
        s.filed,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN company_seed sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K', '10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2019 AND 2024
),
latest_filings AS (
    SELECT * FROM ranked_filings WHERE rn = 1
),
annual_values AS (
    SELECT
        sc.display_name AS company,
        sc.canonical_name,
        lf.cik,
        lf.fiscal_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities',
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations',
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS cfo,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment',
            'PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS capex
    FROM latest_filings lf
    JOIN num n
      ON n.adsh = lf.adsh
     AND n.ddate = lf.period
    JOIN company_seed sc USING (cik)
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations',
        'PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment',
        'PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY sc.display_name, sc.canonical_name, lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
filtered AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        fiscal_year,
        cfo,
        ABS(capex) AS capex_outlay,
        cfo - ABS(capex) AS free_cash_flow,
        CASE
            WHEN cfo IS NULL OR capex IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN cfo <= 400000000 THEN NULL
            WHEN ABS(capex) < 200000000 THEN NULL
            ELSE LEAST(GREATEST((cfo - ABS(capex)) / NULLIF(cfo, 0), -1.0), 1.2)
        END AS fcf_retention_ratio,
        CASE
            WHEN cfo IS NULL OR capex IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN cfo <= 400000000 THEN NULL
            WHEN ABS(capex) < 200000000 THEN NULL
            ELSE LEAST(ABS(capex) / NULLIF(cfo, 0), 1.2)
        END AS capex_intensity_ratio
    FROM annual_values
),
company_trend AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) AS years_available,
        ROUND(AVG(fcf_retention_ratio), 2) AS avg_fcf_retention,
        ROUND(AVG(capex_intensity_ratio), 2) AS avg_capex_intensity,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2019,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2020,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2021,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2022 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2022,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2023,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END), 2) AS retention_2024,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN capex_intensity_ratio END), 2) AS capex_intensity_2024,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN free_cash_flow END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS fcf_2024_billions,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN capex_outlay END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS capex_2024_billions
    FROM filtered
    GROUP BY company, canonical_name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) >= 5
       AND MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END) IS NOT NULL
       AND MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN fcf_retention_ratio END) IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    name,
    years_available,
    avg_fcf_retention,
    avg_capex_intensity,
    retention_2019,
    retention_2020,
    retention_2021,
    retention_2022,
    retention_2023,
    retention_2024,
    capex_intensity_2024,
    fcf_2024_billions,
    capex_2024_billions
FROM (
    SELECT
        company AS name,
        canonical_name,
        years_available,
        avg_fcf_retention,
        avg_capex_intensity,
        retention_2019,
        retention_2020,
        retention_2021,
        retention_2022,
        retention_2023,
        retention_2024,
        capex_intensity_2024,
        fcf_2024_billions,
        capex_2024_billions,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY canonical_name
            ORDER BY avg_fcf_retention DESC NULLS LAST, company
        ) AS name_rank
    FROM company_trend
    WHERE avg_fcf_retention IS NOT NULL
) ranked
WHERE name_rank = 1
ORDER BY avg_fcf_retention DESC NULLS LAST, name
LIMIT 8;

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Rank IT companies by combined dividends plus buybacks and summarize payout ratio shifts versus operating cash flow.
expected_answer.format: Ranking table with annual capital returns and payout ratios
expected_answer.visualization: Stacked bar of dividends + buybacks with payout ratio line overlay
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cik,
        name AS display_name,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cik ORDER BY name) AS rn
    FROM companies

),
company_seed AS (

    FROM sector_companies

),
ranked_filings AS (
    SELECT
        s.adsh,
        s.cik,
        CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        s.period,
        s.filed,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN company_seed sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K', '10-K/A')

),
latest_filings AS (
    SELECT * FROM ranked_filings WHERE rn = 1
),
annual_raw AS (
    SELECT
        sc.display_name AS company,
        sc.canonical_name,
        lf.cik,
        lf.fiscal_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'PaymentsOfDividends' THEN ABS(n.value) END) AS dividends_all,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock' THEN ABS(n.value) END) AS dividends_common,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock' THEN ABS(n.value) END) AS buybacks,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities',
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations',
            'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations'
        ) THEN ABS(n.value) END) AS cfo
    FROM latest_filings lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    JOIN company_seed sc USING (cik)
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'PaymentsOfDividends',
        'PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock',
        'PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY sc.display_name, sc.canonical_name, lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
annual_payouts AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        cik,
        fiscal_year,
        GREATEST(COALESCE(dividends_all, 0), COALESCE(dividends_common, 0)) AS dividends,
        COALESCE(buybacks, 0) AS buybacks,
        CASE WHEN cfo >= 5000000000 THEN cfo ELSE NULL END AS cfo,
        GREATEST(COALESCE(dividends_all, 0), COALESCE(dividends_common, 0)) + COALESCE(buybacks, 0) AS total_return
    FROM annual_raw
),
filtered_payouts AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        cik,
        fiscal_year,
        dividends,
        buybacks,
        total_return,
        CASE
            WHEN cfo IS NULL OR cfo = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE LEAST(total_return / cfo, 4)
        END AS payout_ratio
    FROM annual_payouts
    WHERE total_return >= 2000000000
),
company_trends AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        canonical_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) AS years_available,
        ROUND(AVG(total_return) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS avg_return_billions,
        ROUND(AVG(payout_ratio), 2) AS avg_payout_ratio,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN total_return END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS return_2020,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN total_return END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS return_2021,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2022 THEN total_return END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS return_2022,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN total_return END) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS return_2023,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN payout_ratio END), 2) AS payout_ratio_2020,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN payout_ratio END), 2) AS payout_ratio_2023,
        ROUND(
            (
                MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN total_return END)
                - MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN total_return END)
            ) / 1000000000.0,
            2
        ) AS change_since_start
    FROM filtered_payouts
    GROUP BY company, canonical_name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) >= 4
       AND MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2020 THEN total_return END) IS NOT NULL
       AND MIN(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2023 THEN total_return END) IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    name,
    years_available,
    avg_return_billions,
    avg_payout_ratio,
    return_2020 AS return_2020,
    return_2021 AS return_2021,
    return_2022 AS return_2022,
    return_2023 AS return_2023,
    change_since_start,
    payout_ratio_2020 AS payout_ratio_2020,
    payout_ratio_2023 AS payout_ratio_2023
FROM (
    SELECT
        company AS name,
        canonical_name,
        years_available,
        avg_return_billions,
        avg_payout_ratio,
        return_2020,
        return_2021,
        return_2022,
        return_2023,
        change_since_start,
        payout_ratio_2020,
        payout_ratio_2023,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY canonical_name
            ORDER BY avg_return_billions DESC NULLS LAST, company
        ) AS rn
    FROM company_trends
    WHERE avg_return_billions IS NOT NULL
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY avg_return_billions DESC NULLS LAST, name
LIMIT 8;

      AND CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) BETWEEN {start_year} AND {end_year}
      AND s.period BETWEEN DATE '{start_period}' AND DATE '{end_period}'
),
latest_quarters AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM quarterly_filings
    WHERE filing_rank = 1
),
raw_cfo AS (
    SELECT
        l.cik,
        l.fiscal_year,
        l.fp,
        DATE_TRUNC('day', l.quarter_end) AS quarter_end,
        COALESCE(
            MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities' THEN n.value END),
            MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations' THEN n.value END),
            MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations' THEN n.value END)
        ) AS cfo_ytd
    FROM latest_quarters l
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = l.adsh AND n.ddate = l.quarter_end
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations',
        'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesExcludingDiscontinuedOperations'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY l.cik, l.fiscal_year, l.fp, l.quarter_end
),
ordered_quarters AS (
    SELECT
        r.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY r.cik, r.fiscal_year
            ORDER BY r.quarter_end
        ) AS quarter_index,
        LAG(r.cfo_ytd) OVER (
            PARTITION BY r.cik, r.fiscal_year
            ORDER BY r.quarter_end
        ) AS prev_cfo_ytd
    FROM raw_cfo r
    WHERE r.cfo_ytd IS NOT NULL
),
quarterly_cfo AS (
    SELECT
        o.cik,
        o.fiscal_year,
        o.fp,
        o.quarter_end,
        CASE
            WHEN o.quarter_index = 1 THEN o.cfo_ytd
            WHEN o.prev_cfo_ytd IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE o.cfo_ytd - o.prev_cfo_ytd
        END AS cfo_quarter
    FROM ordered_quarters o
),
filtered_series AS (
    SELECT
        sc.company_name AS company,
        sc.canonical_name,
        qc.quarter_end,
        qc.fiscal_year,
        qc.fp,
        qc.cfo_quarter
    FROM quarterly_cfo qc
    JOIN selected_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE qc.cfo_quarter IS NOT NULL
      AND ABS(qc.cfo_quarter) <= {max_abs_cfo}
      AND qc.quarter_end BETWEEN DATE '{start_period}' AND DATE '{end_period}'
),
coverage AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        COUNT(*) AS quarters_observed
    FROM filtered_series
    GROUP BY canonical_name
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= {min_quarters}
),
final_series AS (
    SELECT
        fs.company,
        fs.canonical_name,
        fs.quarter_end,
        fs.fiscal_year,
        fs.fp,
        fs.cfo_quarter / {value_scale} AS cfo_quarter_scaled
    FROM filtered_series fs
    JOIN coverage c USING (canonical_name)
)
SELECT
    company,
    quarter_end,
    fiscal_year,
    fp AS fiscal_period,
    ROUND(cfo_quarter_scaled, 3) AS operating_cfo_billions
FROM final_series
ORDER BY quarter_end, company
LIMIT {result_limit};

questions.question: Which Technology companies increased EBITDA margins the most between FY2021 and FY2024?
questions.business_context: Identify capital-efficient tech franchises

expected_answer.answer_pattern: Rank Technology companies by FY2021 vs FY2024 EBITDA margin improvement, where EBITDA = OperatingIncomeLoss + Depreciation & Amortization and margin = EBITDA / Revenue.

expected_answer.visualization: Bar chart showing EBITDA margin delta by company.
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH sector_candidates AS (
    SELECT
        c.cik,
        c.name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c.cik
            ORDER BY
                CASE WHEN UPPER(c.name) LIKE '% INC%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
                LENGTH(TRIM(c.name)),
                UPPER(c.name)
        ) AS rn
    FROM companies c
    WHERE LOWER(c.gics_sector) LIKE LOWER('%Technology%')
),
sector_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cik,
        name,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name
    FROM sector_candidates
    WHERE rn = 1
),
ranked_filings AS (
    SELECT
        s.adsh,
        s.cik,
        CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        s.period,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy ORDER BY s.filed DESC) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K','10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN 2021 AND 2024
),
latest_filings AS (
    SELECT adsh, cik, fiscal_year, period
    FROM ranked_filings
    WHERE rn = 1
),
annual_values AS (
    SELECT
        lf.cik,
        lf.fiscal_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'OperatingIncomeLoss',
            'IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS operating_income,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization',
            'DepreciationAndAmortization',
            'DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet',
            'AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets',
            'Depreciation'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS depreciation,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag IN (
            'Revenues',
            'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax',
            'SalesRevenueNet',
            'NetSales'
        ) THEN n.value END) AS revenue
    FROM latest_filings lf
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = lf.adsh AND n.ddate = lf.period
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'OperatingIncomeLoss',
        'IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest',
        'DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization',
        'DepreciationAndAmortization',
        'DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet',
        'AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets',
        'Depreciation',
        'Revenues',
        'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax',
        'SalesRevenueNet',
        'NetSales'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
margin_series AS (
    SELECT
        sc.canonical_name,
        ANY_VALUE(sc.name) AS display_name,
        av.fiscal_year,
        AVG((COALESCE(av.operating_income, 0) + COALESCE(av.depreciation, 0)) / NULLIF(av.revenue, 0)) AS ebitda_margin,
        MAX(av.revenue) AS revenue
    FROM annual_values av
    JOIN sector_companies sc USING (cik)
    WHERE av.revenue IS NOT NULL
      AND av.operating_income IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY sc.canonical_name, av.fiscal_year
),
aggregated AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        ANY_VALUE(display_name) AS display_name,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2021 THEN ebitda_margin END) AS margin_2021,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN ebitda_margin END) AS margin_2024,
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2024 THEN revenue END) AS revenue_2024
    FROM margin_series
    GROUP BY canonical_name
)
SELECT
    display_name AS name,
    ROUND(margin_2021 * 100, 2) AS margin_2021_pct,
    ROUND(margin_2024 * 100, 2) AS margin_2024_pct,
    ROUND((margin_2024 - margin_2021) * 100, 2) AS improvement_pp,
    ROUND(revenue_2024 / 1000000000.0, 2) AS revenue_2024_billions
FROM aggregated
WHERE margin_2021 IS NOT NULL
  AND margin_2024 IS NOT NULL
  AND revenue_2024 >= 2000000000
  AND ((margin_2024 - margin_2021) * 100) >= 5
ORDER BY improvement_pp DESC,
         revenue_2024_billions DESC,
         name
LIMIT 10;

expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH provided_companies AS (

list_candidates AS (

    FROM companies c
    JOIN provided_companies pc
      ON REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(c.name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') = pc.canonical_name
),
combined_companies AS (
    SELECT cik, display_name FROM list_candidates
    UNION ALL
    SELECT cik, display_name FROM sector_candidates
),
company_dim AS (
    SELECT
        cik,
        ANY_VALUE(display_name) AS display_name
    FROM combined_companies
    GROUP BY cik
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT
        s.adsh,
        s.cik,
        CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        s.period,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy
            ORDER BY s.filed DESC, s.period DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS rn
    FROM sub s
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K', '10-K/A')
      AND s.fy BETWEEN {start_year} AND {end_year}
),
latest_filings AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM annual_filings
    WHERE rn = 1
      AND period IS NOT NULL
),
annual_values AS (
    SELECT
        lf.cik,
        lf.fiscal_year,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue' THEN n.value END) AS cash_and_equivalents,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'CashCashEquivalentsAndShortTermInvestments' THEN n.value END) AS cash_and_short_term,
        MAX(CASE WHEN n.tag = 'Assets' THEN n.value END) AS total_assets
    FROM latest_filings lf
    JOIN num n
      ON n.adsh = lf.adsh
     AND n.ddate = lf.period
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue',
        'CashCashEquivalentsAndShortTermInvestments',
        'Assets'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
    GROUP BY lf.cik, lf.fiscal_year
),
normalized AS (
    SELECT
        av.cik,
        av.fiscal_year,
        COALESCE(av.cash_and_equivalents, av.cash_and_short_term) AS cash_balance,
        av.total_assets
    FROM annual_values av
),
ratios AS (

        cd.display_name AS company,
        n.fiscal_year,
        n.cash_balance,
        n.total_assets,
        CASE

    FROM normalized n
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
),
coverage AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cash_to_assets_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN fiscal_year END) AS ratios_available
    FROM ratios
    GROUP BY company
)
SELECT
    r.company,
    r.fiscal_year,
    ROUND(r.cash_balance / 1000000000.0, 2) AS cash_billions,

WHERE r.cash_to_assets_ratio IS NOT NULL

questions.question: Show year-over-year ROE for NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Texas Instruments from 2019 to 2024.
questions.business_context: Evaluate semiconductor capital efficiency

expected_answer.format: Annual ROE table with supporting commentary
expected_answer.visualization: Multi-series line chart plus ROE detail table
expected_answer.sample_analysis:
WITH provided_companies AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM (VALUES ('NVIDIA CORP'),('ADVANCED MICRO DEVICES INC'),('INTEL CORP'),('TEXAS INSTRUMENTS INC')) AS t(company_name)
),
company_dim AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c.cik,
        pc.company_name AS requested_name,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(c.name)), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') AS canonical_name,
        c.name AS dataset_name
    FROM companies c
    JOIN provided_companies pc
      ON UPPER(c.name) = UPPER(pc.company_name)
),
annual_filings AS (
    SELECT
        s.adsh,
        s.cik,
        CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        s.period,
        s.filed,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY s.cik, s.fy
            ORDER BY s.filed DESC
        ) AS filing_rank
    FROM sub s
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
    WHERE s.form IN ('10-K', '10-K/A', '20-F')
      AND CAST(s.fy AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2019 AND 2024
),
latest_filings AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM annual_filings
    WHERE filing_rank = 1
),
annual_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        cd.requested_name AS company,
        cd.canonical_name,
        CAST(l.fiscal_year AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
        COALESCE(
            MAX(
                CASE
                    WHEN n.tag = 'NetIncomeLoss'
                    THEN n.value
                END
            ),
            MAX(
                CASE
                    WHEN n.tag = 'ProfitLoss'
                    THEN n.value
                END
            ),
            MAX(
                CASE
                    WHEN n.tag = 'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic'
                    THEN n.value
                END
            )
        ) AS net_income,
        COALESCE(
            MAX(
                CASE
                    WHEN n.tag = 'StockholdersEquity'
                    THEN n.value
                END
            ),
            MAX(
                CASE
                    WHEN n.tag = 'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest'
                    THEN n.value
                END
            )
        ) AS equity
    FROM latest_filings l
    JOIN num n ON n.adsh = l.adsh
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
    WHERE n.tag IN (
        'NetIncomeLoss',
        'ProfitLoss',
        'NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic',
        'StockholdersEquity',
        'StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest'
    )
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.segments), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(TRIM(n.coreg), '') = ''
      AND COALESCE(n.qtrs, 0) IN (0, 4)
      AND (
          n.ddate IS NULL
          OR EXTRACT(YEAR FROM n.ddate) = CAST(l.fiscal_year AS INTEGER)
      )
    GROUP BY
        cd.requested_name,
        cd.canonical_name,
        l.cik,
        l.fiscal_year
),
coverage AS (
    SELECT
        canonical_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) AS year_count
    FROM annual_metrics
    GROUP BY canonical_name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) >= 6
),
final_series AS (
    SELECT
        am.company,
        am.fiscal_year,
        ROUND(am.net_income / 1e6, 2) AS net_income_millions,
        ROUND(am.equity / 1e6, 2) AS equity_millions,
        ROUND(
            100 * am.net_income
            / NULLIF(am.equity, 0),
            2
        ) AS roe_pct
    FROM annual_metrics am
    JOIN coverage c USING (canonical_name)
    WHERE am.net_income IS NOT NULL
      AND am.equity IS NOT NULL
      AND am.fiscal_year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2024
      AND ABS(
          100 * am.net_income
          / NULLIF(am.equity, 0)
      ) <= 200
)
SELECT
    company,
    fiscal_year,
    net_income_millions,
    equity_millions,
    roe_pct
FROM final_series
ORDER BY company, fiscal_year
LIMIT 200;

        q.fiscal_year,
        q.fp,
        q.revenue,
        q.cost_of_revenue,
        CASE
            WHEN q.revenue IS NULL OR q.revenue = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE (q.revenue - q.cost_of_revenue) / q.revenue
        END AS gross_margin_ratio
    FROM quarter_values q
    JOIN company_dim cd USING (cik)
    JOIN coverage cv USING (cik)
),
ranked_series AS (
    SELECT
        n.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY n.company
            ORDER BY n.period_end
        ) AS seq_asc,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY n.company
            ORDER BY n.period_end DESC
        ) AS seq_desc
    FROM normalized n
),
summary AS (
    SELECT
        company,
        MIN(period_end) AS baseline_period,
        MAX(period_end) AS latest_period,
        MAX(CASE WHEN seq_asc = 1 THEN gross_margin_ratio END) AS baseline_margin,
        MAX(CASE WHEN seq_desc = 1 THEN gross_margin_ratio END) AS latest_margin,
        MAX(CASE WHEN seq_desc = 1 THEN revenue END) AS latest_revenue,
        MAX(CASE WHEN seq_desc = 1 THEN cost_of_revenue END) AS latest_cost,
        COUNT(*) AS quarters_available
    FROM ranked_series
    GROUP BY company
)
SELECT
    rs.company,
    summary.quarters_available,
    summary.baseline_period,
    summary.latest_period,
    ROUND(summary.baseline_margin * 100, 1) AS baseline_margin_pct,
    ROUND(summary.latest_margin * 100, 1) AS latest_margin_pct,
    ROUND((summary.latest_margin - summary.baseline_margin) * 100, 1) AS margin_change_pp,
    ROUND(summary.latest_revenue / 1e9, 2) AS latest_revenue_billions,
    ROUND(summary.latest_cost / 1e9, 2) AS latest_cost_billions,
    rs.period_end,
    rs.fiscal_year,
    rs.fp,
    CONCAT(
        CAST(EXTRACT(year FROM rs.period_end) AS VARCHAR),
        ' Q',
        CAST(EXTRACT(quarter FROM rs.period_end) AS VARCHAR)
    ) AS quarter_label,
    ROUND(rs.revenue / 1e9, 3) AS revenue_billions,
    ROUND(rs.cost_of_revenue / 1e9, 3) AS cost_of_revenue_billions,
    ROUND(rs.gross_margin_ratio * 100, 1) AS gross_margin_pct,
    rs.seq_asc AS quarter_index_asc,
    rs.seq_desc AS quarter_index_desc
FROM ranked_series rs
JOIN summary USING (company)
ORDER BY rs.company, rs.period_end;
